hero.intro: Everything that hangs between the crane hook and the load: spreader beams and frames with published load charts, and lifting beams, frames and attachments engineered for one load.

guidance.heading: Spreader beam or lifting beam?
guidance.body: A spreader beam takes its load at two end points and works in compression, with slings running up to the hook at an angle, so it is light and suits long loads when there is headroom. A lifting beam hangs from one central point and carries the load in bending, so it is heavier but needs little headroom and can carry several bottom points along its length. A spreader frame or H-frame does the same in two directions, for a load lifted at four or more points.

standards.heading: Design standard
standards.body: Below-the-hook lifting attachments are designed to EN 13155. ASME B30.20 and BTH-1 apply where a US design basis is required, and DNV standards for offshore lifting equipment. Every item ships with a declaration of conformity, a test certificate and user instructions.

service.heading: How we quote
service.body: Standard modular beams are quoted from their load charts: give us the load, the span and the sling angle. Engineered equipment starts from the load: its weight, centre of gravity, lifting points and the headroom you have. The maker's engineers issue a general arrangement drawing for approval before anything is made.

items.q: Can I lift from the middle of a spreader beam?
items.a: No. A spreader beam is designed to carry compression between its two end links, and a load hung from a strut would put it in bending. If the load needs a central or intermediate lifting point, use a lifting beam.

The angle each top sling leg makes with the vertical. The larger it is, the more compression the beam carries and the lower its rated load, so spreader beam charts give the load at 45°, 30° and 20° STV and the shortest top sling that keeps the angle within each limit.

items.q: Do these products ship from stock in Dubai?
items.a: No. Standard modular systems ship from the maker's stock and engineered equipment is built to order, so we confirm the lead time with each quotation.

products.title: Modular Spreader Beam — 4 t, 0.5–4.5 m Span
products.descriptionShort: Modular spreader beam rated to 4 t, built from two end units and bolt-in struts to any span from 0.5 m to 4.5 m. The size table is the load chart: rated load and minimum top sling length at 45°, 30° and 20° sling angles for every span.
products.descriptionLong:
A bolt-together spreader beam rated up to 4 t, made of two end units and interchangeable struts. It can be built to any span from 0.5 m to 4.5 m in the steps of its chart, and taken apart again for transport and storage. The beam takes its load at the two end links only and works in compression, so it is light for its capacity and suits long loads lifted at two points.

Span chart

Each row is one span: the rated load at a top sling angle of 45°, 30° and 20° to the vertical, and the shortest top sling leg that keeps the angle within that limit. At 45° the full 4 t is available to a span of 3.5 m; beyond that the chart steps the load down.

The beam is certified for every configuration in its chart, so changing the span does not need a new test or certificate. Pre-use checks and periodic thorough examination still apply.

Components and bolts

Each end unit and link plate is rated 2 t, half the beam's 4 t, because the beam is modular and every component is rated on its own. With an off-centre load, check that neither end carries more than 2 t. Struts join with M10 × 30 grade 8.8 bolts, nuts and washers tightened to 80 Nm; a full set plus spares is supplied. No more than six struts between the end units.

Rules for use

  • Load the beam only at its two end links. Never hang a load from a strut.
  • Keep the top sling angle at 45° to the vertical or less, and read the chart for the angle you rig.
  • End links hang downward, toward the load; bottom slings run vertically to the load.
  • Check that no shackle or sling clashes with the beam.
  • Put the longest strut in the middle, so there is no flange joint at the centre of the beam.

Ordering

Quote the part number of the span you need from the table, or send the load weight, the distance between its lifting points and the hook height, and we will choose the size and span. Top and bottom rigging (shackles, slings and master links) can be quoted with the beam. Custom struts, special end links and tag-line points are available to order.

faqs.question: How do I read the span chart?
faqs.answer: Find the distance between the load's two lifting points in the Span column, then read across to the sling angle you will rig. faqs.answer: A wider top sling angle pushes the end units together harder, so the beam carries more compression for the same load. Long spans at 45° are limited by that compression, which is why the chart steps the load down there.

faqs.question: Can I hang the load from the middle of the beam?
faqs.answer: No. The beam is designed for compression between its two end links; a load on a strut puts it in bending. For a central or intermediate lifting point, use a lifting beam.

faqs.question: Do I need to re-certify the beam when I change the span?
faqs.answer: No. It is certified for every configuration in its chart. It still needs pre-use checks and thorough examination at the intervals your local regulations set.

faqs.question: Is it suitable for offshore use?
faqs.answer: Standard beams are not DNV type approved. Offshore versions with DNV design approval and witnessed testing are made to order; ask when you send the enquiry.

faqs.question: What do I need to send for a quote?
faqs.answer: The load weight, the distance between its two lifting points, the hook height or headroom, and whether you need the rigging as well. We will pick the span and confirm the chart rating at your sling angle.

products.descriptionShort: Modular lattice spreader beams rated 3 t and 6 t for very long, light loads: up to 44 m long with up to 44 lifting connections along the beam. For cladding panels, pipe and structural members.
products.descriptionLong:
A light modular lattice beam for loads that are long rather than heavy. Lattice sections bolt together to the length of the load, and the load hangs from connections along the beam rather than from two ends, so a long flexible item is supported along its length instead of sagging between two points.

The WLL is the total load on the beam. How it shares between the connections depends on the rig, so the rigging is agreed with the order.

Why a lattice

A long load lifted at only two points bends between them, and a solid spreader long enough to avoid that is heavy. A lattice girder is stiff for its weight, so a beam tens of metres long stays light enough to handle with the crane that lifts the load. Sections bolt together, so the same kit builds a short beam for one job and a long one for the next, and breaks down for transport.

Rigging

The beam hangs from top slings to the hook and the load hangs from drop slings at the connection points, set at the spacing the load needs. Keep every drop sling vertical, and keep the top sling angle within the limit given in the user instructions.

Typical loads

  • Long cladding and façade panels
  • Pipe spools and long pipe
  • Steel sections and trusses
  • Blades, masts and other long, flexible items, with cradles

products.descriptionShort: Welded fixed-length spreader beams for repeat lifts, direct-to-hook spreaders and heavy spreaders for monopiles, vessels and long structures, designed around one load and certified to EN 13155.

A fixed spreader beam is welded to one span. products.title: Gantries, Jib Cranes & Davits
products.descriptionShort: Mobile and fixed steel gantries, A-frame and cantilever gantries, runway beams, jib cranes and davits, built to order for the load, span and height, with hoists and trolleys supplied with them.
products.descriptionLong:
Mobile gantries are designed for indoor use on a flat floor, from light units up to 5 t and more, for spans up to 10 m and heights up to 5 m and beyond; their wheels are for positioning only. Fixed gantries, runway beams and supporting structures are built to any capacity, span and height.

Cantilever gantries land a load beyond the support for maintenance or loading a vehicle, and jibs and davits are designed for the reach and height needed, manual or powered. Outdoor units can be galvanized.

Typical builds

  • Mobile A-frame gantries
  • Fixed gantries and runway beams
  • Cantilever gantries
  • Jib cranes
  • Davits
  • Hoists, trolleys and chain blocks to suit

What we need to quote

Send us the load weight and where its centre of gravity sits, the load's length and width, the positions of its lifting points, the crane hook height and any headroom limit, and the environment the equipment will work in (indoor, outdoor, offshore, hazardous area). A drawing, a 3D model or a photo of the load is the quickest way to start.

How it is made and certified

Engineered below-the-hook equipment is built to order. Your enquiry is reviewed by the maker's design engineers, who issue a general arrangement drawing for your approval before anything is made. Each item is designed to EN 1993 for the steel structure, load tested before dispatch and supplied with a declaration of conformity, a test certificate and user instructions. Design calculations, material certificates, NDT records and third-party witnessed testing can be added to the order, and offshore designs to DNV standards are available on request. We confirm the lead time with the quotation.

In service

In service, the equipment gets a pre-use check before every lift and a thorough examination by an approved third party at the interval the site's authority sets: in Abu Dhabi, Code of Practice 34 sets six months for lifting accessories and twelve for lifting equipment, and in Dubai the examination is made by an EIAC-accredited inspection body. Its rated load, identification and test date are marked on it, and the user instructions state how it may and may not be rigged. Our guide to lifting equipment inspection in the UAE sets out the rules emirate by emirate.
